# Notes on deliberate practice

Deliberate practice means working at the edge of your ability, not just repeating what you already know, and it requires focused attention rather than mindless repetition.

Feedback loops should be as short as possible so mistakes are caught early, before they harden into habits that are much harder to unlearn later.

Rest is part of the work; consolidation happens between sessions, which is why cramming everything into one long session is usually counterproductive.
